question: Who was the founder of Tughlaqabad city? (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Feroz Shah Tughlaq
Gahasudin Tughlaq
Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Mahmood Tughlaq
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq

Explanation:
The city of Tughlaqabad was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq in 1321 AD. He was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, which ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1320 to 1325. Tughlaqabad Fort is a historic fort located in Delhi, built by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq as his capital. The city is known for its massive walls and strong architecture. Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq's tomb is also situated in Tughlaqabad. During his reign, administrative reforms were implemented and the army was strengthened.

Explanation:
तुगलकाबाद शहर की स्थापना गयासुद्दीन तुगलक़ ने 1321 ई. में की थी। वह तुगलक वंश का संस्थापक था, जिसने दिल्ली सल्तनत पर 1320 से 1325 तक शासन किया। तुगलकाबाद किला दिल्ली में स्थित एक ऐतिहासिक दुर्ग है, जिसे गयासुद्दीन तुगलक़ ने अपनी राजधानी के रूप में बनवाया था। यह शहर अपनी विशाल दीवारों और मजबूत संरचना के लिए जाना जाता है। गयासुद्दीन तुगलक़ का मकबरा भी तुगलकाबाद में स्थित है। उनके शासनकाल में प्रशासनिक सुधार किए गए और सेना को मजबूत किया गया।

question: Hampi was the capital of the __________ Kingdom. (RRB NTPC CBT-I (31/01/2021) Shift 1)

solution:

Explanation:

question: Manyakheta was the capital of which of following dynasties during the eighth century AD? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (16/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Rashtrakuta
Pratiharas
Chera
Pala
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rashtrakuta

Explanation:
During the 8th century AD, Manyakheta (present-day Malkhed, Karnataka) was the capital of the Rashtrakuta dynasty. The Rashtrakutas initially had their capitals at Halihippi and Nasirabad, but later shifted to Manyakheta. Dantidurga (735-756 AD) founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty. The most famous ruler, Amoghavarsha I (814-878 AD), patronized Kannada literature and authored the 'Kavirajamarga'. The Rashtrakutas of Manyakheta participated in the tripartite struggle for Kannauj against the Palas and Pratiharas. Their reign saw architectural marvels like the Kailash Temple at Ellora, built during Krishna I's rule. The dynasty declined after the death of Krishna III in 973 AD, succeeded by the Western Chalukyas.

question: In Delhi Sultanate, the holder of an ‘iqta’, who also worked as the administrative head of his ‘iqta’, was designated as ________. (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: muqti
qazi
ariz
wazir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is muqti

Explanation:
During the Delhi Sultanate, the iqta system was a key administrative and revenue arrangement. Under this system, the state assigned land revenue rights to officials or soldiers in lieu of salary, and such land was called an iqta. The holder of the iqta was known as muqti or iqtadar. The muqti was responsible not only for collecting revenue from his iqta but also for maintaining law and order, administration, and military management within his territory. Qazi was a judicial officer, ariz was the head of the military department, and wazir was the prime minister in charge of finance and administration. Hence, the holder of an iqta who served as its administrative head was designated as muqti.

☛ What was the main purpose of the iqta system? → Assigning land in lieu of salary
☛ What was the main function of a muqti? → Administration and revenue collection of iqta
☛ What was the role of wazir in the Delhi Sultanate? → Head of finance and administration

question: Who among the following was the ruler of Gujarat when Humayun attacked the kingdom in 1532? (RRB JE CBT-I 2024 (17/12/2024) Shift 3)

question: By which of the following dynasties was the Brihadeswara temple built? (RPF Constable 2024 (18/03/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following monuments was built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah is said to be built to commemorate the eradication of plague? (RRB NTPC Tier I (02/04/2016) Shift 2)
options: Alai Minar
Charminar
Fateh Buxj
Qutub Minar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Charminar

Explanation:
The Charminar was built in 1591 AD by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah. It is located in Hyderabad, Telangana. It is said to have been constructed to commemorate the end of a plague epidemic in the city. question: The famous composition 'Totinama' was created during the reign of _____________.   (RPF SI 2018 (11/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Babar
​Akbar
​Aurangzeb
Humayun
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Akbar

Explanation:
'Totinama' (or 'Tuti-nama') is a Persian illustrated manuscript containing 52 miniature paintings. It was created during the reign of the Mughal emperor Akbar. The book is a Persian translation of the Sanskrit text 'Shuka-Saptati' (Seventy Tales of the Parrot), originally written by Ziyauddin Nakhshabi. Akbar's reign was a golden age for Persian literature and miniature painting. The Mughal atelier, under the supervision of masters like Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad, produced this exquisite work. The 'Totinama' reflects the early Mughal painting style, blending Persian and Indian elements. Akbar established a royal library (Kitabkhana) where many important texts were translated and illustrated, and 'Totinama' is one of the most notable surviving examples from this period.

question: Pala Rulers were primarily great patrons of which religion/sect? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (02/12/2024) Shift 3)

The founder of the dynasty, Gopala, adopted Buddhism, and his successors, especially Dharmapala and Devapala, contributed significantly to the construction of Buddhist monasteries and universities. They followed Mahayana Buddhism and also encouraged Tantric Buddhism (Vajrayana). Thus, Buddhism was the primary religion patronized by the Pala rulers, while other religions like Vaishnavism, Shaivism, and Jainism were tolerated but not given as much patronage.
